claim: what the GPU actually does when a pure-AR wave carries 2 rows instead of 1
command: for W in 1 2: env HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIPENGINE_EXECUTION_PROFILE=production HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/he-rows/hipcc-version.txt rocprofv3 -f csv -o ar$W -d /tmp/he-rows/tr$W --kernel-trace -- .venv/bin/python scripts/gguf_c1c8_ar_only_control.py --width $W --model /models/gguf/Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --output /tmp/he-rows/ar-$W.json --max-tokens 24; then .venv/bin/python scripts/gguf_rocprof_width_scale_diff.py --base-dir /tmp/he-rows/tr1 --candidate-dir /tmp/he-rows/tr2 --rows-base 1 --rows-candidate 2 --top 22 --json /tmp/he-rows/scale-diff.json; hipcc --version > /tmp/he-rows/hipcc-version.txt is run outside the profiler first
command_provenance: The numbers were produced by the /tmp predecessor of scripts/gguf_c1c8_ar_only_control.py (same _request_mtp_value patch, same harness argv). The published command above names the committed script, promoted after the run so the route is reproducible and gate-clean.
conclusion: 2x rows costs 1.40x wall per step, and 92% of that growth is GPU kernel time (1.355x). It decomposes into ~9.9 ms/step of extra PREFILL work (the two prompts in a wave pay near-full prefill scaling: 5.7 s -> 10.4 s) and ~6.5 ms/step of extra decode, with the decode route itself amortizing well at 1.24x for double the rows. The residual non-kernel per-step time grows only 2.4 -> 5.4 ms. So the C2 deficit is a prefill/admission-cost problem, not a decode-amortization failure - which promotes task #12 (prefill fixed cost) to the highest-value GGUF lever and retires the 'batch the decode GEMVs' hypothesis with a mechanism.

deadlock_reproduced_and_fixed: two earlier attempts hung with the GPU idle: a `hipcc --version` probe stuck and its parent blocked in wchan=anon_pipe_read. HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 alone does NOT prevent it - the builder still probes to compute the cache key. hipengine/core/build.py prescribes the PAIR: require_cached AND HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE (or an explicit compiler_version). With both, no probe is spawned and the trace completes.

mechanism_followup.decision_point_narrowed: the route is not chosen by resolve_gguf_linear_dispatch: for LAYOUT_GGUF_Q4_K_T16 every rows>1 resolves t16_wmma_prefill_bf16_bf16_out regardless of HIPENGINE_GGUF_Q4K_ROWTILE (pinned by tests/test_runtime_gguf_linear_q4k_rowtile_knob.py). The env is consumed one level down at the launch sites - launch_gguf_linear (gguf_linear.py:2447), launch_gguf_linear_pair (:4182), launch_gguf_linear_pair_silu (:4658) - which matches the widest width-2 kernel being a *dual* (pair-route) rowtile launch. Caveat added after the A/B: those launch sites are reached only when no session has pinned the flag, and the resident serving route does pin it, so HIPENGINE_GGUF_Q4K_ROWTILE does not steer the shipping AR decode path at all.
mechanism_followup.single_thread_established: both traces run every kernel on one worker thread (width 1: thread 869469 carries 308,889 'other' + 137,632 width-1-route launches; width 2: thread 873535 carries 314,977 + 164,460 rowtile + 9,792 width-1-route). The only other thread has 322 launches / ~6 ms. So the width-2 route difference is not an artifact of a second arm running on its own thread - the control's nominal MTP arm shares the serving thread.
mechanism_followup.still_unresolved: which predicate inside those launch sites prefers rowtile over the WMMA fallback at rows 2..8, and whether that preference is optimal, is still unexplained. An order-controlled A/B on HIPENGINE_GGUF_Q4K_ROWTILE at width 2 is running to answer the optimality half.
mechanism_followup.why_this_matters_for_the_original_claim: the headline decomposition (prefill +9.9 ms/step, decode 1.24x for 2x rows) does not depend on any of this; only the sentence 'rows>=2 switches the decode route wholesale' was stated as observed-not-explained, and it remains observed.

mechanism_found: rows>=2 switches the decode route wholesale: the width-1 families (q4_k_t16_dense_single_local32, q4_k_t16_dense_dual_local32_single_lane, q6_k_t16_qmicro_planar_gemv_bf16_*, qk_t16_selected_direct_gemv) collapse to ~7% of their launches, and 18 *_rowtile_* kernels appear that never run at rows=1 (q4_k_t16_dense_dual_rowtile_single_lane 4774 ms / 31232 launches at grid 139264; q4_k_t16_dense_rowtile_gemv_kernel 1914 ms / 50752; q6_k_t16_qmicro_planar_gemv_rowtile 2026+990+744 ms; q5_k_t16_dense_rowtile_gemv 1508 ms; q4_k_t16_dense_rowtile_residual 1219 ms). Unmeasured question worth a microbenchmark: is the rowtile route the cheapest way to do 2 rows, given the width-1 families cost 28.2 ms/step for 1 row and rowtile costs 32.7 for 2?
route: GGUF direct (hipengine.dispatch.gguf_linear); engine AR with mtp_max_draft=0 and both sessions' mtp_enabled forced False

route_ab_invalid.design: four pure-AR width-2 packets in ON,OFF,OFF,ON order via scripts/gguf_c1c8_ar_only_control.py, medians over 20 cells each (both arms AR, mtp_engaged=0/40 verified).
route_ab_invalid.invalid_reason: the env never reached the route. A traced width-2 run with HIPENGINE_GGUF_Q4K_ROWTILE=0 shows 164,798 rowtile launches vs 164,460 at the default - the same kernels. Precedence is kwarg > session > env (gguf_linear.py:1516) and the resident serving route opens the session, so the env only moves plain bench calls. Pinned by tests/test_runtime_gguf_linear_q4k_rowtile_knob.py.
route_ab_invalid.not_a_finding: this is not evidence that the two routes are equivalent, and not evidence that rowtile is optimal. It is a null with a known cause.
route_ab_invalid.question: is the rows 2..8 rowtile route cheaper than the WMMA fallback it exists to avoid?
route_ab_invalid.result: on: 32.028 (position 1), 31.332 (position 4); off: 31.675 (2), 31.518 (3). Mode means 31.680 vs 31.597 (+0.26%), and the sign flips between position pairs, so no mode effect was visible.
route_ab_invalid.useful_byproduct_measured: process-position bias quantified at width 2: the same setting measured first vs last in the sequence differed 32.028 -> 31.332 = 2.2%. The changelog has been quoting '~1-2 points of same-protocol drift' as a rule of thumb; this is a direct measurement of it under an order-controlled design.
route_ab_invalid.what_would_answer_the_question: force the route in code (a test-only seam at launch_gguf_linear_pair) or microbenchmark the two kernel families directly at Q4_K_M shapes; an env A/B cannot reach it on the server route.

supersedes_detail: The earlier artifact's per-token numbers are not disputed. What this trace contradicts is its mechanism reading - 'weights are not amortised across rows' and its live hypothesis that decode runs per-row GEMV kernels. On the same model, decode changes route wholesale at rows>=2 and the route serving 2 rows costs 1.24x the route serving 1 row, so decode kernel time does amortize; the extra per-token cost is prefill scaling inside the wave, not un-amortized weights. Scope: only widths 1 and 2 are traced, so the 1.62x (C3) and 2.69x (C8) figures in that artifact are not explained here.
workload: pure AR forced on both arms of scripts/gguf_mtp_c1c8_server_bench.py via scripts/gguf_c1c8_ar_only_control.py, 10 prompts x 24 tokens, median of 3 runs, one traced process per width
